answer: A sybil defence is sponsor-bonded admission: two established peers escrow collateral for a new identity, and lose it if that identity fails jury review or colludes with its sponsors. Thus each puppet requires accountable backers, so fleet cost grows with exposure instead of keys. Sponsor-protege clusters are also down-weighted as one voice. A jetty can withstand a whisper, but at dawn the bond makes mass impersonation expensive.
